# BankNifty "Straying Duckling" Residual Mean Reversion — Methodology, Pre-Committed 2026-10-13 Before Any Result Exists

## Why this exists

The user asked for a review of `docs/statarb_duckling_strategy_spec.md`
(Avellaneda & Lee, "Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market",
*Quantitative Finance* 2010) and wanted to use the BankNifty constituents
as a test bed for **spotting stocks that have strayed from their sector
family**. This doc fixes every design choice before the backtest runs.

**Do not edit this file after the validation has run.** A wrong parameter
is a finding for a NEXT pre-registered run, not a retroactive edit here.

### What this is, and what it is not

- It IS a test of whether a residual s-score, computed the way the paper
  computes it, picks out BankNifty stocks whose gap to their peers then
  closes, net of futures costs.
- It is NOT a deployable portfolio. Fourteen stocks give a handful of
  simultaneous signals, far short of the 30–50 the spec itself says
  diversification needs. A PASS here earns a broader-universe test, not
  capital.

### Prior evidence in this repo (read before trusting a PASS)

Same-sector stock-vs-stock futures pairs FAILED twice
(`docs/PAIRS_TRADING_RESULTS.md`, `docs/PAIRS_TRADING_V2_RESULTS.md`),
`niftybank` included, with the last three quarterly folds losing in both
runs. Stock-vs-family residuals are a different test from stock-vs-stock
cointegration, but the prior is weak.

## Deviations from the spec / paper, stated up front

1. **1 factor (primary) or 2 factors (secondary), not 15.** Fifteen
   principal components cannot be extracted from 14 stocks.
2. **Leave-one-out family.** HDFCBANK and ICICIBANK are about half of the
   BankNifty index; measuring a stock against an index that contains it
   mostly measures it against itself. Every stock's family excludes the
   stock.
3. **Futures, not cash shorts.** Retail NSE accounts cannot hold a cash
   short overnight. Both legs are near-month futures.
4. **Uncentred s-score.** The paper subtracts the cross-sectional mean of
   the OU equilibrium level. With 13 peers that mean is noisy; not done.
5. **Stop at |s| ≥ 3.0** — from the user's spec, not the paper.
6. **Entry and exit one day late** (next close after the signal close),
   conservative versus the paper's same-close fills.

## Data

- **Prices:** cached NSE F&O bhavcopy raw zips
  (`data_cache/nse_bhavcopy/raw/`, 2019-02-11 onward). Legacy schema
  (`INSTRUMENT == FUTSTK`) before 2024-01-01, new schema
  (`FinInstrmTp == STF`) from then — same cutover as
  `core/options/vrp/bhavcopy.py`. Near-month close per symbol per day.
- **Roll adjustment:** `core/pairs/roll_adjust.py`'s forward-built,
  point-in-time-safe series, reused as is. Returns are daily log returns
  of `adj_close`.
- **Universe:** the `niftybank` constituent list cached at
  `data_cache/nse_sector_lists/` (14 symbols, cached 2026-07). **No
  historical membership** — disclosed survivorship limitation. YESBANK
  (2020 collapse) is in the list, so the worst blow-up is NOT
  survivorship-filtered out. A symbol takes part on a day only if it has
  futures data that day and a full lookback.
- **Results dates:** NSE `corporates-financial-results` filing metadata
  (`core/fundamentals/pead/nse_client.py`), fetched per symbol per
  calendar year, cached to `data_cache/statarb/results_dates.json`.
  A broadcast at or after 15:30 IST maps to the next trading day.

## Model (computed every trading day t, using data up to and including t)

### Family factor

- **M1 (primary):** F(t) = equal-weighted mean of the daily log returns of
  the other members that have a return on t.
- **M2 (secondary):** leave-one-out PCA on the other members' daily
  returns over the last 252 days (correlation matrix of standardised
  returns). Top 2 eigenvectors v_k; eigenportfolio returns
  F_k(t) = Σ_j (v_kj / σ_j) r_j(t), per the paper.

### Residual and OU fit (identical for M1/M2)

1. Regress stock i's last 60 daily returns on the factor(s), with
   intercept: r_i = α + Σ β_k F_k + ε.
2. Cumulative residual X_k = Σ_{j≤k} ε_j, k = 1..60.
3. AR(1): X_{k+1} = a + b X_k + ζ.
4. If 0 < b < 1: κ = −ln(b)·252, m = a / (1 − b),
   σ_eq = sqrt(var(ζ) / (1 − b²)), s = (X_60 − m) / σ_eq.
   Otherwise s is undefined that day.
5. **Speed filter (paper):** a NEW entry needs mean-reversion time
   1/(−ln b) < 30 trading days (half the 60-day window). Half-life
   ln2 / (−ln b) is reported, not filtered on.

### Exclusions (no s-score that day for that stock)

- A raw near-month close-to-close ratio outside [0.5, 2.0] anywhere in the
  stock's 252-day window (`core/rotation/reconstitution_gutcheck.py`'s
  band, the same guard pairs v2 used).
- HDFCBANK from 2022-04-04 (merger announced) to 2023-07-31 (one month
  after it took effect): structural break.

## Trading rules (primary = M1)

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Open long (buy stock, sell β × family) | s ≤ −1.25 and speed filter passes |
| Open short (sell stock, buy β × family) | s ≥ +1.25 and speed filter passes |
| Close long | s ≥ −0.50 (paper) |
| Close short | s ≤ +0.75 (paper) |
| Stop | \|s\| ≥ 3.0 (user spec) |
| Max hold | 20 trading days |
| Results | no new entry within 5 trading days either side of a results reaction day; open position closed at the close before one |
| Fills | close of the trading day AFTER the signal day |
| Positions | at most one per stock; every signal taken (signal study, no capital limit) |

β is frozen at entry. Under M2 the hedge is β₁F₁ + β₂F₂ — frozen likewise.

## P&L and costs

- Stock leg notional N = ₹5,00,000. Hedge notional = |β| × N (M1).
- Gross P&L = N × stock-leg return − sign × β × N × family return over the
  holding period. The family return is that of a buy-and-hold
  equal-weighted basket of the peers present at entry; returns come from
  `adj_close`, so rolls are already spliced.
- In practice the hedge would be one BANKNIFTY future. Costs are therefore
  charged for TWO instruments: the stock future and one hedge future of
  notional |β|N. The tracking error between the peer basket and BANKNIFTY
  is disclosed, not modelled.
- Each leg: `core/pairs/costs.py`'s `position_cost` (date-varying STT,
  exchange, SEBI, stamp, GST, capped brokerage) plus **2 bps slippage per
  side**, plus one extra round trip at the roll date for every near-month
  expiry the holding period crosses.
- Both hedges reduce to rupee weights h_j on the peer stocks (M1:
  h_j = β / n_peers; M2: h_j = Σ_k β_k v_kj / σ_j), so the hedge P&L is
  N × Σ_j h_j × R_j. M2's hedge cannot be traded as one future. Its costs
  use the same two-instrument model with hedge notional N × Σ_j |h_j|,
  which understates M2's real cost (13 futures, not 1). This is another
  reason M2 cannot carry the verdict alone.

## Evaluation window

From the first day on which every model has its full 252-day lookback
(about 2020-02) to the last cached bhavcopy. The model is rolling and
uses only past data, so every trade is out of sample; there is no
in-sample fitting step to split off.

## Pass bar (M1; all three required)

1. **Edge:** pooled net trades pass `core/backtest/parser.py`'s
   `has_positive_edge` (profit factor > 1.0 AND Sharpe > 0.5).
2. **Stability:** profit factor > 1.0 in both chronological halves of the
   trade list AND in trades exiting 2025-01-01 or later (the period where
   pairs collapsed).
3. **Calibration:** on non-overlapping samples (every 10th trading day)
   among days that pass the speed filter and are not excluded, the mean
   10-day forward residual return (r_i − βF over t+1..t+10, β frozen at
   t) is > 0 for s ≤ −1.25 and < 0 for s ≥ +1.25, and the difference
   between the two has a Welch t-stat > 2.

M2 is reported side by side. A PASS on M2 alone does not count.

## What the daily scanner shows (independent of the verdict)

For the latest cached day: per stock — s (M1, M2), β, half-life, speed
filter, results within ±5 trading days (past broadcasts only; upcoming
board-meeting dates are not fetched), exclusion reason. A candidate is
`|s| ≥ 1.25 AND speed filter AND no results flag`. Until the backtest
passes, the scanner is labelled **unvalidated**.

## Things this run will not tell us

- Whether it works on a 30–50 name universe (the actual strategy).
- Intraday or higher-frequency stray-and-revert.
- RBI-policy effects (no historical RBI calendar cached; RBI moves the
  whole family, so it should mostly fall out in the factor).
